item.title: What’s a Cabin Cruise? Everything You Need to Know Before Booking
item.description: Imagine waking up to the sound of water gently lapping against the hull, stepping outside, and diving straight into a clear, turquoise ocean. For a long time, enjoying a holiday like this meant you either needed a lifetime of sailing experience or the budget to rent a whole private vessel with a captain. Now, travelers can book a cabin cruise and experience the magic of a sailing vacation to an exotic destination for the price of a single hotel room. Even better, sailing experience is not required. You simply book your cabin, step aboard, and leave the work to the crew on board the yacht. Before you pack your bags and head for the marina, here is everything you need to know about this effortless way to explore the world. What Is a Cabin Cruise? A cabin cruise, also called a by-the-cabin sailing charter , is a style of travel where you rent a private stateroom or cabin on a yacht. The rest of the vessel is shared with a small group of like-minded travelers, so you have opportunities to socialize in between exploring islands and relaxing in your room. Every cabin charter trip features a carefully planned route, shared communal spaces, delicious meals, and a professional crew to run the ship. It’s an easy way to dip your toes into the yachting lifestyle. What Is a Cabin Charter Like? The entire travel process is designed to be stress-free from the moment you book your cabin cruise vacation to the day you head home. Choosing Your Destination and Dates Your journey begins by selecting where you want to sail and picking the dates that fit your schedule. These trips follow set itineraries, which you can view ahead of time. This way, you can see which ports you’ll visit and plan ahead of time. Arrival and Boarding When you arrive at the marina base, the crew will welcome you aboard and show you to your private stateroom. After a quick safety briefing and an introduction to the yacht, the captain casts off the lines and sets sail. Your Cruise Each day follows a relaxing rhythm of sailing, swimming, exploring hidden coves, and enjoying fresh meals on deck. While the captain handles the sailing, you share the spacious decks with your fellow passengers. Do You Need Sailing Experience? With this type of sailing vacation, no experience is required. You do not need to know how to tie a single knot, read a navigation chart, or handle a steering wheel. The price of your cabin includes the services of the captain and crew. They take care of navigation, weather tracking, anchoring, and all daily shipboard operations. The only thing you need to do the entire week is relax and have fun. What’s Included in a Cabin Yacht Charter? Inclusions vary based on the package you choose and the company you book with. Premium options, such as Dream Yacht ’s cabin cruises, typically include: A private, comfortable double cabin with its own bathroom Access to all shared yacht spaces, like the forward trampolines, salon, and sun decks The full services of a professional captain and cook Onboard water toys, which may include things like snorkeling gear, paddleboards, and kayaks Before booking, be sure to check the trip details to confirm inclusions and what you might need to cover during your cruise. Food, Beverages, and Culinary Options Many packages offer a half-board plan, which includes select meals such as breakfast and lunch. With half-board options, you may dine ashore at ports where you drop anchor. Other packages feature a full-board plan, which means breakfast, lunch, and dinner are included. Optional Excursions and Extras Depending on where you are sailing, you might have the option to add on excursions like guided island hikes and historical tours. It is always a good idea to check your specific package details before booking, so you know exactly what is covered and what extras you might want to explore. item.title: Are you qualified for a bareboat yacht charter?
item.description: If you want to go on a sailing vacation but are unsure if your sailing experience means you are qualified for a bareboat yacht charter, we’ve got some tips and advice for you. Your safety is important to us and it’s important that you are able to handle your yacht in your chosen destination. For bareboat yacht charters, we expect you to have experience sailing a boat of similar size. It’s also helpful to have at least one crew member of similar experience. For most destinations, you do not need bareboat charter certification. Learn more about our bareboat yacht charters . Getting ready for sailing We usually ask that you have sailing experience on a boat of similar size. It’s also helpful to have at least one crew member of similar experience. While a bareboat charter certificate is not usually mandatory, safety is always our #1 priority. Even if you’re highly experienced, we recommend that you take sailing courses from reputable organizations. Refresh your knowledge on anchoring, navigation, maneuvering a large sailboat in a tight marina, and other nuances of bareboat chartering. If you are still unsure of your sailing abilities, or simply want the knowledge of a local skipper, you can hire a professional captain at a daily rate, then continue on your own when you feel comfortable. If you’d rather not cook, hire a chef and have all of your meals prepared for you. Contact us for more information. Finding the right destination for your sailing experience You will find information on the local cruising ground, wind systems and weather conditions on our destination pages . Our expert team can help you if you want to know the level of experience required for your chosen destination and if you are qualified for a bareboat yacht charter. Contact our team . We can advise where to find line of sight navigation and calm waters. Also, we can help if you are looking for a challenge. The British Virgin Islands are popular because of the calm waters and easy navigation. If you’re after a relaxing sailing vacation, try Corfu and Lefkas in Greece as the Ionian Islands offer plenty of short leg island hopping. Our bases in the Exumas and Australia’s Whitsunday Islands are good for sailors who don’t want an energetic sail. Sailors seeking more of a challenge can look for bareboat yacht charters from our Cyclades Islands bases in Paros and Mykonos in Greece, with its Meltemi wind system. Croatia , with its Bora wind, can also offer some fast sailing conditions at the right time of year. When do you need an accredited sailing license? Bareboat certification is not usually mandatory in most destinations, but you need to check the specific license requirements of your chosen destination to know if you are qualified for a bareboat yacht charter. What about Europe? Some destinations, particularly in the Mediterranean, require official sailing certification or licensure from a recognized organization, such as an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or equivalent qualification. Our destination base guides indicate if you need a recognized sailing license. In these cases, the local authorities may require the skipper to prove their bareboat sailing proficiency. The skipper will need to take original copies of their bareboat certification with them on charter. Before you book your charter vacation, ensure that you have the required sailing certification that is accepted by the country you are sailing in. Unsure about your destination’s requirements? Contact our team . What if I don’t have proof of competence? If you don’t have the right bareboat certification for your chosen destination, you can always add a skipper , which offers many benefits. Skippers have excellent local knowledge and the best recommendations for local anchorages and restaurants to make the most of your vacation. item.title: Hotspots for scuba diving in Thailand
item.description: While Thailand may be best known for its tropical climate, white sand beaches, rich culture and delicious cuisine, scuba divers know it as a world-class diving and snorkeling destination. The stunning waters of Thailand are home to over 300 islands, 1200 miles of coastline and hundreds of incredibly diverse dive sites. From impressive wrecks to pristine reefs to colorful coral-encrusted walls, scuba diving in Thailand will delight every diver from novice to expert. One of the most exciting ways to experience diving in Thailand is from aboard a private sailing charter, where you can avoid the crowded day charter boats and dive directly from your liveaboard yacht. The Dream Yacht Charter base is located in Yacht Haven Marina on the island of Phuket that extends down into southeast Thailand’s Andaman Sea – where most of Thailand’s top dive and snorkeling spots can be found. Scuba diving in Thailand is known and loved for exceptional underwater visibility, varied marine life and some of the best coral to be found anywhere in the world. And if you’re anything like the many divers looking to experience a thrilling dive with whale sharks and manta rays, the Andaman Sea can provide the dive experience of a lifetime. When putting together your itinerary for scuba diving in Thailand, consider the time of year, your dive experience, and the types of activities you enjoy most – whether you want to swim with tiger sharks, snorkel along scenic beaches, or macro dive and linger among rare tiny sea critters. When diving the Andaman Sea, visiting between October and April is ideal, when seas are calmer and visibility is at its best. To help you plan, we’ve put together our list of favorite hotspots for scuba diving in Thailand. Read on to find your diving bliss! Phi Phi Islands A NOVICE DIVERS PLAYGROUND The Phi Phi Islands are stunningly beautiful both above and below the surface. With its sparkling bays and crescent beaches surrounded by stunning rock formations, it’s one of the most photographed areas of Thailand. It’s worth a visit for the above-water scenery alone, but for divers the underwater experience is a must. With striking coral gardens, caverns, and swim-throughs, along with calm novice-friendly bays, it offers some of the most thrilling diving for beginners. Keep an eye out for leopard sharks that are often seen here. Koh Phi Phi is also a great option for those interested in snorkeling in Thailand. Check out the main island of Koh Phi Phi Don for amazing snorkeling at both Nui Beach and Long Beach. Phuket CONVENIENT GATEWAY TO THAILAND DIVING Phuket is often overlooked when considering the many options for scuba diving in Thailand. But Phuket’s coastline offers a surprising variety of dives with dramatic underwater landscapes, excellent visibility and easy conditions. And it’s one of the best places in Thailand for those interested in shore diving for beginners. Visit the popular Koh Dok Mai dive site to see extraordinary yellow tube corals and numerous eels. More experienced divers will enjoy Shark Point, known for beautiful leopard shark sightings. Richelieu Rock AN ADVANCED DIVER’S PARADISE Some say the Richelieu Rock dive site offers the best scuba diving in Thailand. This pinnacle site is located north of the Similan Islands, and is fairly remote, taking a bit longer to reach. But it’s well known for whale shark sightings, with the best time of year to spot them being between February and May. And even if you don’t spot the whale sharks, Richelieu Rock has much more to offer, including manta rays, walls of yellow anemones, and macro critters like sea horses, and porcelain crabs. Keep in mind that Richelieu Rock is best for advanced divers, due to the open water swells and strong currents.
